input: Someone just rear-ended me at a traffic light. Car is drivable, no one hurt. What do I do?
expected:
I'm sorry that happened, and I'm glad nobody was hurt. Here's what to do now:
1. Swap names, phone numbers, addresses, registration numbers and insurer details with the other driver.
2. Take photos of both cars, the damage, the road and the other car's number plate.
3. Note the time, place and any witnesses' contact details.
4. Don't admit liability or agree who was at fault at the scene.
Then start a claim in the portal under Claims > Start a claim, ideally within 24 hours. The claims team will take it from there.

input: does my home insurance cover a burst pipe? water everywhere in the kitchen
expected: I'm sorry, that's stressful. First, turn off the water at the main stop tap and switch off the electricity if water is near sockets or appliances. Home policies usually cover sudden escape of water, such as a burst pipe, but not gradual leaks or wear and tear. Your policy wording is the final word, and the claims team decides on cover. Take photos of the damage and the pipe, keep receipts for emergency repairs and start a claim under Claims > Start a claim.

input: I'm in Thailand and my son broke his arm, we're at a hospital and they want payment upfront
expected: I'm sorry, I hope your son is okay. Please call our 24/7 emergency assistance line now. The number is in the portal under Help > Emergency abroad and on your policy card. They can talk to the hospital directly about payment and guarantee fees where your policy allows. Keep every receipt and medical report. I've also passed your message to our team so they know you're in touch.

input: what's my excess?
expected: Your excess is the part of a claim you pay yourself, and it's shown on your policy schedule. To find it, go to Portal > Documents > Policy schedule. Some policies have different excesses for different claim types, such as a higher one for escape of water or for young drivers, so check the line for the type of claim you have in mind.

input: Can I add my wife as a driver on my car policy? She's 34 with a clean licence
expected:
Yes, you can add a named driver at any time:
1. Go to Portal > My policy > Make a change > Add a driver.
2. Enter her details and driving history.
3. The portal will show any change to your premium before you confirm.
The change starts from the date and time you choose, and an updated certificate will appear in Documents.

input: I need proof of no claims for my new insurer, how do I get it
expected: You can download it yourself: go to Portal > Documents > Proof of no-claims discount. It shows how many claim-free years you've built up with us. If it isn't there yet, for example because your policy only ended in the last few days, let me know and I'll ask our team to email it to you.

input: My claim has said 'in review' for 3 weeks. What's going on?? CLM-20931
expected: I'm sorry for the wait on claim CLM-20931. "In review" means the claims team is checking the claim against your policy and the evidence sent in. Sometimes they're waiting on a report, quote or document. I've passed your message to the claims team and asked them to update you, and someone will contact you within 1 business day with where things stand and anything they still need from you.

input: You rejected my claim and it's outrageous. I've paid you for 9 years. I want this reviewed.
expected: I'm sorry, I understand how disappointing this is after nine years with us. You have every right to ask for the decision to be reviewed. I've passed your request to our team as a formal complaint, and someone will contact you within 1 business day. If you have extra evidence, such as photos, reports or receipts, have it ready, as it can help the review.

input: Does travel insurance cover cancelling my trip if my mum is sick?
expected: Many travel policies cover cancellation when a close relative is seriously ill, usually with a doctor's letter confirming it, but this depends on your policy level and on whether the illness was already known when you bought the cover. Check the cancellation section in Portal > Documents > Policy wording. If you need to cancel, start a claim under Claims > Start a claim and the team will confirm what's covered.

input: hi i want to cancel my policy, bought it 5 days ago, found cheaper
expected: No problem. You're within the 14-day cooling-off period, so you'll get a full refund as long as you haven't made a claim. Go to Portal > My policy > Cancel policy and choose the date. The refund goes back to the account you paid from, usually within 5–7 business days.

input: My car was stolen from outside my house last night
expected: I'm really sorry. If you haven't yet, report the theft to the police and get a crime reference number. Then start a claim under Claims > Start a claim and add the reference number. Because this is a vehicle theft, I've also passed it to our claims team, and someone will contact you within 1 business day to guide you through the next steps and tell you which documents they need, such as keys and the vehicle registration document.

input: how much would it cost to add my teenager to my car insurance
expected: I can't quote prices in chat, but you can see the exact cost before committing. Go to Portal > My policy > Make a change > Add a driver and enter their details. The new premium shows before you confirm, and you can back out at no cost if you decide not to go ahead.

input: i moved house, need to update address. also is my bike covered in the new garage?
expected: Thanks for letting us know. To update your address, go to Portal > My policy > Make a change > Change address. Any price change shows before you confirm. As for your bike, contents policies often cover bicycles kept in a locked garage, but some have a limit per bike or need high-value bikes listed separately. Check "Bicycles" in your policy wording, and if your bike is worth more than the single-item limit, add it in the same Make a change menu.

input: I missed my direct debit payment, will my insurance be cancelled?
expected: Thanks for getting in touch quickly. A single missed payment doesn't cancel your policy straight away. We'll try to collect it again and write to you first. To avoid any gap in cover, check your bank details under Portal > Payments, or make a one-off payment there. If you're struggling to pay, tell me and I'll put you in touch with our team about options.

input: is flood covered in my area? I live near a river
expected: Most home policies include flood cover as standard, but some properties in high-risk areas have special terms or a higher flood excess. Your policy schedule will show any special terms under "Endorsements". You can find it in Portal > Documents > Policy schedule. If you're unsure what it means for your home, I can pass your question to our team.

input: A tree fell on my roof in the storm!! hole in the roof, rain coming in, kids are scared
expected:
I'm so sorry, that sounds frightening. If anyone is in danger or the structure looks unsafe, leave the area and call emergency services. Then:
1. Keep everyone away from the damaged rooms.
2. If it's safe, protect belongings from the rain.
3. Arrange emergency repairs, such as a tarpaulin, and keep the receipts.
4. Take photos.
I've passed this to our claims team as urgent. They'll contact you within 1 business day, and you can also start the claim under Claims > Start a claim.

input: Phone screen cracked, does my home contents cover it?
expected: It depends on whether your policy includes accidental damage or personal possessions cover away from home. Basic contents cover usually doesn't include a dropped phone. Check your policy schedule in Portal > Documents for "Accidental damage" or "Personal possessions". If either is listed, you can start a claim under Claims > Start a claim, and the claims team will confirm cover and any excess.

input: Can you just tell me if my claim will be approved? It's for water damage from my upstairs neighbour.
expected: I can't say whether a claim will be approved, because the claims team makes that decision based on your policy wording and the evidence. Damage caused by water escaping from a neighbour's property is a common type of home claim, though. Gather photos, any repair quotes and your neighbour's contact details, then start the claim under Claims > Start a claim. If your neighbour's insurer is involved, the claims team will handle that contact too.

input: my renewal price went up 40%!! why?? no claims
expected: I understand that's a big jump, and I'm sorry it's a surprise. Prices can change at renewal for reasons beyond your own claims, such as repair costs, claims in your area or changes to your car or home. I can't go through pricing in chat, but I've passed your question to our team, and someone will contact you within 1 business day to explain it and check your options. You can also switch off auto-renewal in the portal while you decide.

input: Do I need to tell you about a speeding ticket?
expected: Yes. Please tell us about motoring convictions, including speeding points, for anyone on the policy. Not disclosing them can affect a future claim. Go to Portal > My policy > Make a change > Add a conviction. Any change to your premium shows before you confirm.

input: Where can I find my certificate of insurance? Police asked for it
expected: You can download it straight away: go to Portal > Documents > Certificate of insurance. It's a PDF you can show on your phone or print. If you can't log in, let me know and I'll ask our team to email it to the address on your policy.

input: I lost my luggage on my flight to Lisbon. Airline says they're looking.
expected: Sorry, that's a rough start to a trip. First, make sure you have the airline's Property Irregularity Report (PIR) reference. Keep receipts for essentials you buy while you wait. Most policies cover reasonable essentials after a delay, and lost items if the bag isn't found, minus anything the airline pays. If the bag isn't returned, start a claim under Claims > Start a claim with the PIR, your boarding pass and receipts.

input: I think my neighbour is making a fake claim against me for a fence. what should I do
expected: Thanks for letting us know. Please don't agree to pay anything or admit responsibility to your neighbour directly. I've passed this to our claims team, who handle third-party claims and look into anything that seems suspicious. Someone will contact you within 1 business day. In the meantime, keep any photos, messages or other evidence about the fence.

input: Hello, I'm 82 and I find the website confusing. I just want to know when my policy ends.
expected: Hello, thank you for getting in touch, and I'm happy to help. Your policy end date is printed on your policy schedule and on the renewal letter we post to you about three weeks beforehand. I've also asked our team to call you, so someone can tell you the date and talk you through anything else. They'll be in touch within 1 business day.

input: is my dog covered on my home insurance if he bites someone
expected: Home policies usually include personal liability, which can cover your legal liability if your pet injures someone, but some policies exclude certain dog breeds or dogs used for business. Check the "Liability" section in Portal > Documents > Policy wording. If something has already happened, please tell me and I'll pass it to our team, and don't admit liability to the other person in the meantime.

input: I'd like to speak with a human please, not a bot.
expected: Of course. I've passed your request to our team, and someone will contact you within 1 business day. If you tell me briefly what it's about, such as a claim, payment or policy change, I'll add it to the note so you don't have to explain twice.
